entries.title: Acts 28:1
segments: And when we were escaped, we ascertained that the island was called Malta.

entries.title: Acts 28:2
segments: The foreign-speaking people showed us uncommon kindness, for they lighted a fire and made us all welcome, because of the rain and because of the cold.

entries.title: Acts 28:3
segments: Now when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and thrown them on the fire, a viper crawled out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

entries.title: Acts 28:4
segments: When the natives saw the reptile hanging on his hand, they began saying to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet justice does not allow him to live."

entries.title: Acts 28:5
segments: However, he shook off the reptile into the fire and received no harm.

entries.title: Acts 28:6
segments: But they kept expecting him to swell up or fall down dead suddenly. But after waiting a long time, and seeing no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said over and over that he was a god.

entries.title: Acts 28:7
segments: Now in the neighborhood there were estates belonging to the governor of the island, whose name was Publius. He received us and entertained us for three days courteously.

entries.title: Acts 28:8
segments: It happened however that the father of Publius was lying ill of fever and dysentery. So Paul went to see him and prayed and laid his hands on him and healed him.

entries.title: Acts 28:9
segments: After this all the other sick people on the island came, and continued to be restored to health.

entries.title: Acts 28:10
segments: These loaded us with many honors and, when at last we set sail, they put on board such things as we needed.

entries.title: Acts 28:11
segments: Three months passed before we set sail an Alexandrian ship which had wintered in the island. Its name was "The Twin Brothers."

entries.title: Acts 28:12
segments: And touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

entries.title: Acts 28:13
segments: From thence, tacking round, we reached Rhegium. Next day a south wind sprang up, which brought us in a day to Puteoli.

entries.title: Acts 28:14
segments: There we found brothers who invited us to stay a week with them. Then we reached Rome.

entries.title: Acts 28:15
segments: From there the brothers, when they heard about us, came out to meet us as far as the Appian Forum and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them he thanked God and took courage.

entries.title: Acts 28:16
segments: When we finally entered Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself with the soldier to guard him.

entries.title: Acts 28:17
segments: Now three days later he called the leading Jews together, and when they were come together he said to them: "Brothers, I was delivered a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of your fathers.

entries.title: Acts 28:18
segments: "Then when they had examined me they wanted to set me at liberty because there was no cause of death in me.

entries.title: Acts 28:19
segments: "But when the Jews objected I was forced to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything to accuse my nation of.

entries.title: Acts 28:20
segments: This is the reason why I begged you to see and speak with me. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain."

entries.title: Acts 28:21
segments: They said to him: "We neither received any letters about you from Judea nor has any brother come hither to report or speak any harm of you.

entries.title: Acts 28:22
segments: "But we are eager to hear from you what it is that you believe; for we all know that as for this sect it is everywhere spoken against."

entries.title: Acts 28:23
segments: So they arranged a day with him and came to him in his lodgings in great numbers. He expounded the matter to them; testifying to the Kingdom of God, and persuading them about Jesus, from morning till evening, both from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets.

entries.title: Acts 28:24
segments: Some began to believe what he said, but some were unbelieving.

entries.title: Acts 28:25
segments: Unable to agree among themselves, they began to go, but not before Paul had spoken a word to them, saying: "Right well did the Holy Spirit say to your ancestors, through the prophet Isaiah:

entries.title: Acts 28:26
segments: "Go to the people and tell them, You will hear and hear, and by no means understand; And will look, and by no means see.

entries.title: Acts 28:27
segments: For this people's heart is grown obtuse, Their ears are heavy of hearing, Their eyes have they closed, Lest they should see with their eyes And hear with their ears, Lest they understand with their heart, And turn again, and heal them.

entries.title: Acts 28:28
segments: "Be fully assured, therefore, that this salvation of God is now sent unto the Gentiles. They will listen to it."

entries.title: Acts 28:29
segments: When he finished speaking, the Jews departed, and reasoned among themselves.

entries.title: Acts 28:30
segments: After this Paul lived for two whole years in his own rented house, and used to receive all who came to see him.

entries.title: Acts 28:31
segments: He continued to preach the kingdom of God, and to teach about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, quite unmolested.
